abstract: Rare subcellular structures are difficult to retain during lamella preparation for cryo-electron tomography, particularly in high-pressure-frozen specimens. Here we introduce two complementary workflows for three-dimensional fluorescence-guided milling on a commercial cryo-focused ion beam-scanning electron microscope with integrated fluorescence imaging. Iterative fluorescence correlation uses repeated rounds of imaging and milling to refine the target position, whereas bidirectional fluorescence correlation images a lifted-out block from two orthogonal directions. We validated both by targeting centrosomes in waffle-frozen early Caenorhabditis elegans embryos, each of which occupy approximately 0.007% of the embryo volume. We recovered recognizable centrosomes in 83% and 67% of lamellae examined by transmission electron microscopy, respectively, compared with 25% using a refined, 2D-guided high-throughput SOLIST workflow, run as a benchmark. Neither method requires hardware modification or fluorescent fiducial beads. These workflows provide accessible strategies for targeting rare subcellular structures during lamella preparation, with or without a lift-out hardware.
